questions.text: What does a phi function represent at a control-flow join in SSA?

options.A: A runtime test that executes every incoming path before the join.
options.B: A value selected from incoming definitions according to the predecessor taken.
options.C: A memory load that restores the original source variable name.
options.D: A branch that discards all but the most recently decoded predecessor.

questions.explanation: SSA gives each definition a unique name. A phi merges the definitions reaching a join, selecting the value associated with the actual incoming control-flow edge.

questions.text: A temporary holds load32(p), then a store to p occurs before its only use in the same block. Should the simplifier replace that use with a fresh load32(p)?

options.A: Yes, because one use makes any substitution safe.
options.B: Yes, because SSA names guarantee memory never changes.
options.C: No, because loads can never appear inside expressions.
options.D: No, because the intervening store can change the loaded value.

questions.explanation: Moving a load past a store can observe a different value. The lesson blocks load substitution across intervening stores or calls.

questions.text: collect_params computes count = max(argument-register indexes read at entry, default=-1) + 1, then takes that prefix of [rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9]. If only rsi is read at entry, which parameters does it produce?
questions.explanation: rsi has index 1, so count is 2 and slicing the register order takes both rdi and rsi.
